subject: Pilot offboarding & termination-for-convenience concession request
messages:
From: priyom.das@redwood.com
To: contracts@acme.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot offboarding & termination-for-convenience concession request

Hi Jared / Acme contracts team,

Thanks again for piloting Redwood Inference — we appreciate the engagement and the feedback from your ML team. We're preparing the Order Form for signature but hit a small snag on the Term and Termination-for-Convenience language in Section 2.2 and the auto-renew clause. Before legal redlines get heavy, wanted to propose a pragmatic compromise to keep the deal moving:

- For pilot-level Order Forms (<= 3 months, non-production), Redwood can accept a shorter notice window: 30 days written notice to not auto-renew.
- For paid pilots converting to committed production seats, standard 45-day notice and mutual 60-day termination-rights remain.
- If Acme needs a mutual 60-day window today, we can do that in exchange for a 45-day pro-rated termination credit (covering unused committed months) or a one-time conversion credit applied to the first invoice.

I've attached the latest draft Order Form (Acme_OrderForm_draft_v3.pdf) and a short summary of the redline delta (redline_summary.xlsx). Can your team confirm which path they'd prefer (30-day pilot carveout vs. mutual 60-day with credit)? If you prefer we can inline a short amendment clause for signature.

Next steps: if you confirm direction, I'll loop Legal (Kim) for clean redlines and send a DocuSign powerform for quick execution.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Acme_OrderForm_draft_v3.pdf (Order Form draft), redline_summary.xlsx (summary)

From: contracts@acme.com
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acme.com
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot offboarding & termination-for-convenience concession request

Hi Priyom,

Appreciate the pragmatic approach. Acme's standard procurement stance is to keep a 60-day written notice for termination for convenience on all paid engagements, even pilots that carry monetary commitment, to give internal teams time to wind down usage and budgets.

If Redwood can offer a pro-rated refund (or credit) for unused committed months in the event of a TFC trigger, we may be able to accept a slightly shortened notice. Would you be willing to propose concrete language that we can send to internal Legal?

I've attached our internal procurement note for context (Acme_internal_req.pdf).

Thanks,
Jared Meyers
Sr. Counsel, Acme Corp
jared@acme.com

Attachments: Acme_internal_req.pdf

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: priyom.das@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot offboarding & termination-for-convenience concession request

Priyom / Karthik — quick legal note before we send anything external.

High-level guidance:
- We're comfortable carving out a 30-day opt-out for true "pilot" Order Forms that explicitly state pilot scope/duration and do not include production SLAs or committed capacity. That should be a controlled exception in the Order Form (pilot flag + end date).
- For anything that converts to production or includes a term commitment, we should preserve a mutual 60-day termination-for-convenience right OR accept 45-day notice with a commercial concession (credit/refund) as you suggested.
- Auto-renew: do not allow automatic renewal on pilot-level docs. Auto-renew should require affirmative customer confirmation for pilots. For production contracts, auto-renew may proceed but must include an explicit reminder and notice window (e.g., 60 days prior).

Suggested redline excerpt to propose to Acme: "If the Order Form is designated as a 'Pilot' (defined as a written Order Form with an explicit pilot end date and no production SLAs), Customer may terminate this Order Form for convenience with thirty (30) days' prior written notice. For all other Order Forms, termination for convenience shall require sixty (60) days' prior written notice. If Customer exercises termination for convenience on a non-pilot Order Form after the initial committed term, Customer will receive a pro-rated credit for the unused portion of prepaid fees, or as otherwise agreed in writing."

Attachments: legal_redline_brief.docx (annotated extract).

Commercial ask: Sales should confirm whether Redwood is willing to offer the one-time conversion credit if Acme insists on 60-day notice before we accept the shorter notice window. If Sales confirms, Legal will prepare a clean amendment and powerform for signature.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
kim...@redwood.com

From: priyom.das@redwood.com
To: contracts@acme.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 8 Oct 2025 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot offboarding & termination-for-convenience concession request

Hi Jared — thanks, this is helpful. Per Legal guidance below, here's a concise commercial proposal to put to Acme procurement:

Option A (Pilot carveout):
- Pilot Order Forms (<= 3 months, explicitly designated) — 30 days' written notice to not renew; no auto-renew; no termination fee.

Option B (Committed or production):
- Standard mutual 60-day TFC. Alternatively, Customer may elect a 45-day notice in exchange for a one-time conversion credit equal to the remaining prorated committed fees (applied as a credit to the next invoice).

If that works for Acme we'd like confirmation and we'll produce a short amendment for signature. I've opened the HubSpot deal record for traceability (HS-623412) and will send a DocuSign powerform once you confirm the option.

DocuSign (proposed): https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?env=na1&acct=12345678&ppid=abcd1234

Can you confirm which option Acme prefers? If you want the 60-day window as-is, Kim is prepared to accept the one-time conversion credit to expedite.

Best,
Priyom
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: jared@acme.com
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acme.com
Date: Wed, 8 Oct 2025 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot offboarding & termination-for-convenience concession request

Priyom / Kim — thank you. Acme is willing to accept Option B with the 45-day notice + one-time conversion credit applied to the first post-termination invoice. That provides the runway our internal teams need while giving Redwood the commercial protection you requested.

Please send the short amendment and the Order Form redline via DocuSign and we'll route for signature. Attached is a marked copy of the procurement note confirming the internal OK (signed_markup.pdf).

Regards,
Jared Meyers
Sr. Counsel, Acme Corp
jared@acme.com
